text: analytical bias corrections misclassification rates known:
code: set.seed(42) n <- 5000 z_true <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4) x1 <- rnorm(n) y <- rpois(n, exp(0.8 * z_true - 0.5 + 0.7 * x1))  # Introduce misclassification p01 <- 0.10; p10 <- 0.15 z_hat <- z_true z_hat[z_true == 0] <- rbinom(sum(z_true == 0), 1, p01) z_hat[z_true == 1] <- 1 - rbinom(sum(z_true == 1), 1, p10)  Pi <- matrix(c(1 - p01, p01, p10, 1 - p10), 2, 2) df3 <- data.frame(y = y, z = factor(z_hat), x1 = x1)  fit <- mcglm(y ~ mc(z, Pi) + x1, data = df3, family = "poisson",              method = c("naive", "bca", "bcm", "cs"), pi_z = 0.4) fit #>  #> Call: #> mcglm(formula = y ~ mc(z, Pi) + x1, data = df3, family = "poisson",  #>     method = c("naive", "bca", "bcm", "cs"), pi_z = 0.4) #>  #> Family: poisson  |  n = 5000, K = 2, p = 3 #> Methods: naive, bca, bcm, cs #>  #> Coefficients: #>         NAIVE    BCA      BCM      CS      #> gamma    0.6272   0.7843   0.8367   0.8400 #> alpha0  -0.4113  -0.4988  -0.5280  -0.5353 #> alpha1   0.7134   0.7136   0.7137   0.7137 #>  #> Degrees of Freedom: 5000 Total (i.e. Null);  4997 Residual #> Null Deviance:     9252  #> Residual Deviance: 5660  | AIC (naive): 12590

text: Let \(Y_i\) denote scalar response, \(x_i \\mathbb{R}^r\) vector cleanly observed covariates (typically including intercept), \(Z_i \\{0, 1, \dots, K-1\}\) latent categorical regressor observed proxy \(\hat Z_i\). binary case (\(K = 2\)) let \(\xi_i = (Z_i, x_i^\top)^\top\) \(\hat\xi_i = (\hat Z_i, x_i^\top)^\top\); \(K > 2\), \(Z_i\) dummy-encoded baseline category 0 \(\xi_i = (d_i^\top, x_i^\top)^\top\). parameter \(\psi = (\gamma^\top, \alpha^\top)^\top\), \(\gamma \\mathbb{R}^{K-1}\) coefficients (dummy-coded) latent regressor \(\alpha \\mathbb{R}^r\) coefficients \(x_i\). conditional mean \(E[Y_i | Z_i, x_i] = \mu(\psi^\top \xi_i)\) \(\mu = g^{-1}\) inverse canonical link. Misclassification mechanism. \(K = 2\), mechanism summarized false-positive rate \(p_{01} = \Pr(\hat Z = 1 \mid Z = 0)\), false-negative rate \(p_{10} = \Pr(\hat Z = 0 \mid Z = 1)\) prevalence \(\pi = \Pr(Z = 1)\). \(K > 2\), \(K \times K\) matrix \(\Pi_{j\ell} = \Pr(\hat Z = j - 1 \mid Z = \ell - 1)\) (column-stochastic) prevalence vector \((\pi_0, \dots, \pi_{K-1})\). Misclassification assumed nondifferential: \(\hat Z \perp\!\!\!\perp (Y, x) \mid Z\). Estimators. Let \(\hat\psi\) solve proxy score \(\hat U_n(\psi) = n^{-1} \sum_i \hat\xi_i \{Y_i - \mu(\psi^\top \hat\xi_i)\} = 0\) (naive GLM estimator). Define per-observation drift \(m_i(\psi) = (-c_1 \delta_i(\psi),\, -c_2 \delta_i(\psi)\, x_i)^\top\) \(\delta_i(\psi) = \mu(\gamma + \alpha^\top x_i) - \mu(\alpha^\top x_i)\), \(c_1 = p_{01}(1 - \pi)\) \(c_2 = p_{01}(1 - \pi) - p_{10} \pi\), let \(\hat (\psi) = n^{-1} \sum_i \dot\mu(\psi^\top \hat\xi_i) \hat\xi_i \hat\xi_i^\top\) \(\hat M(\psi) = \partial \hat m / \partial \psi^\top\). : BCA: \(\hat\psi_{\mathrm{bca}} = \hat\psi - \hat (\hat\psi)^{-1} \hat m(\hat\psi)\) BCM: \(\hat\psi_{\mathrm{bcm}} = \hat\psi - (\hat (\hat\psi) + \hat M(\hat\psi))^{-1} \hat m(\hat\psi)\) CS: solves \(n^{-1} \sum_i \phi_i(\psi) = 0\)     \(\phi_i(\psi) = \hat\xi_i \{Y_i - \mu(\psi^\top \hat\xi_i)\} - m_i(\psi)\) one-step: maximizes integrated mixture likelihood     \(\prod_i \sum_\ell \pi_\ell\, \Pi_{\hat z_i+1, \ell+1}\, f(Y_i \mid Z = \ell, \psi)\)     automatic differentiation (RTMB). Multicategory analogues replace \((p_{01}, p_{10}, \pi)\) \((\Pi, \pi_z)\) throughout; see Appendix B Battaglia et al. (2025) explicit formulas. Inference. five estimators report asymptotic variance vcov.mcglm: \(^{-1} C ^{-1}\) naive / BCA / BCM (Theorems two-step expansion bias-corrected estimators drifting misclassification), \(J^{-1} S J^{-\top}\) CS (Z-estimator sandwich, \(J = -(\hat + \hat M)\), \(S = E[\phi_i \phi_i^\top]\)), inverse Hessian integrated log-likelihood one-step. See vcov_corrected alternative, conservative BCA/BCM sandwich.
